oop.why: Model shared identity and framework hierarchies.
oop.useWhen: Domain types, UI, and libraries that expect classes.

gen.why: Type-safe collections without boxing every value.

malloc.reason: Ordinary objects are GC-allocated. Pointers and stackalloc exist only in unsafe/native interop, not as the language heap.

gc.why: Throughput and safety over explicit free.

sources.quote: In the common language runtime (CLR), the garbage collector (GC) serves as an automatic memory manager.

trace.fragment: generational mark/relocate/compact (gen0–2 plus LOH); not reference counting
trace.why: Collect short-lived objects without walking the whole heap.
trace.price: You profile generations; you rarely pick the algorithm in source.

sources.quote: A garbage collection has the following phases: A marking phase that finds and creates a list of all live objects.

rc.reason: Managed heap is tracing GC. COM AddRef is interop, not the language heap.

sources.quote: The garbage collector uses this list to create a graph that contains all the objects that are reachable from the roots.

own.reason: No borrow checker. IDisposable is a pattern for unmanaged cleanup, not unique ownership in the type system.

sources.quote: For most of the objects your application creates, you can rely on garbage collection to perform the necessary memory management tasks automatically.
